qs.q:
Match each message (1–5) and its meaning (A–F).
There is one letter that you do not need.

0. Something's come up about the conference in Munich. Really important. We have to make a decision. Get back to me. [G = We need to talk.]
1. I thought I told you the report was needed by lunchtime today. I don't see it on my desk. I hope you haven't lost it.
2. Tony told me you talked to Sandra this morning and explained the situation. I hope it wasn't too upsetting. Anyway, let me know how she took it.
3. Hey guys. Helena's not well so we've had to call it off. We can think of something else to surprise her.
4. I heard you were called in by the principal. Did he blame you for the broken computer? I'm sure he blew up like a volcano. But relax. He'll forget about it in a few days.
5. I'm a little bit worried about Frank's work on his project. It's way behind schedule. If he doesn't start working faster, he'll be in trouble.
items: 1 — The report was needed by lunchtime. I don't see it on my desk.
2 — Let me know how she took it.
3 — Helena's not well so we've had to call it off.
4 — He blew up like a volcano. But relax. He'll forget about it.
5 — Frank's project is way behind schedule.
rights: C — He needs to hurry up.

The smartest dog in the world

"John Pilley, a retired professor, taught his dog Chaser to understand more than 1,000 words. Chaser is an average-sized border collie with round eyes, mostly the colour of cookies-and-cream ice cream, but with a black patch right above her left eye."

What do we find out about Chaser from the first paragraph?
A She is black around the right eye.
B She likes cookies and ice cream.
C She belongs to a former teacher.
opts: She is black around the right eye.
She likes cookies and ice cream.
She belongs to a former teacher.

qs.q:
The smartest dog in the world

"The farmer responded: 'Tell me why, when I call out my dog Jeb or Fuzz out of four dogs and ask them to go get Molly and Tolly, two sheep out of a hundred, they do it every time?'"

What did a farmer tell Mr Pilley about his dogs?
A His dogs sat with him around the fire.
B His dogs knew the names of the sheep.
C His dogs' names were Molly and Tolly.
opts: His dogs sat with him around the fire.
His dogs knew the names of the sheep.
His dogs' names were Molly and Tolly.

qs.q:
The smartest dog in the world

"Other scientists worked with monkeys showing how fast they learn through play. For Pilley, our connection with dogs was more special. He was sure that working one-on-one rather than with groups of animals must bring even better results."

What did Pilley believe about how dogs learn?
A They learn best when people play with them.
B They learn best when they are in a group.
C They learn best when they are alone.
opts: They learn best when people play with them.
They learn best when they are in a group.
They learn best when they are alone.

qs.q:
The smartest dog in the world

"At the end of the third month of her training, only five-months-old Chaser knew 40 words."

How long did it take Chaser to learn 40 words?
A Two months.
B Three months.
C Five months.

The smartest dog in the world

"For three years, Mr Pilley trained Chaser for four to five hours every day. He showed her an object, said its name up to 40 times, then hid it and asked her to find it."

How did Pilley succeed in training Chaser?
A He trained her several hours a day for three years.
B He showed her 40 objects a day for three years.
C He repeated her name 40 times each day.
opts: He trained her several hours a day for three years.
He showed her 40 objects a day for three years.
He repeated her name 40 times each day.
